- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true prices as baseline.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is > 20% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model may lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 2–3 days to capture sentiment momentum.
